### Headline summary
- The FBI has attributed the record-breaking $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korean hackers known as TraderTraitor. ([Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/fbi-confirms-north-korean-hackers/), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/fbi-links-north-koreas-tradertraitor-to.html))
- Binance has resumed phased customer withdrawals, stating that 90% of the losses are covered, while Bitcoin ETFs saw significant outflows. ([Cointelegraph.com News](https://cointelegraph.com/news/binance-says-phase-one-of-withdrawals-opens-after-63b-hack?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound), [The Guardian Cybercrime](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/01/binance-losses-covered-hack-fbi-north-korea-cryptocurrency))
- Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab server after hackers attempted to exploit a critical vulnerability in its development infrastructure. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/alpine-linux-rebuilds-gitlab-after-attempted-rce-attack/))

### FBI attributes $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea
The FBI has confirmed that North Korean hackers, identified as TraderTraitor, were responsible for the record-breaking $6.3 billion theft from Binance. The agency linked 628 cryptocurrency wallet addresses to the attack and urged private sector cooperation to block money laundering. ([Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/fbi-confirms-north-korean-hackers/), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/fbi-links-north-koreas-tradertraitor-to.html), [Cointelegraph.com News](https://cointelegraph.com/news/fbi-blames-north-korea-for-record-63b-binance-hack?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound), [HackRead](https://hackread.com/fbi-crypto-wallet-addresses-north-korea-binance-hack/))

### Binance resumes withdrawals and investors withdraw funds
Binance has begun phased customer withdrawals following the $6.3 billion hack, stating that 90% of the losses are covered. In the first full trading session after the incident, Bitcoin ETFs saw significant outflows as investors pulled billions in funds. ([Cointelegraph.com News](https://cointelegraph.com/news/binance-says-phase-one-of-withdrawals-opens-after-63b-hack?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound), [The Guardian Cybercrime](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/01/binance-losses-covered-hack-fbi-north-korea-cryptocurrency), [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382309/bitcoin-etf-investors-exits-record-binance-hack), [The Guardian Cybercrime](https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/01/investors-take-out-36bn-from-binance-after-record-hack-that-stole-billions))

### Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20-21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/alpine-linux-rebuilds-gitlab-after-attempted-rce-attack/))

### Hackers Steal About $2.7 Million From Polymarket Traders via Hijacked DebugBear Script
Malicious code on the website of prediction market Polymarket sold some signed-in traders' positions and moved their funds to the hackers on October 29. The code had replaced a page-speed script that the site loaded from an outside company. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-steal-about-27-million-from.html))

### CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
A critical flaw in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud let an attacker log in as a trusted client without holding that client's private key. To do it, the attacker had to reach their HTTPS API over the network and have the trusted client's public certificate. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/critical-lxd-and-microcloud-flaw-cvss.html))

### NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what has been described as a "highly sophisticated infection chain" targeting government organizations in Asia. The activity, detailed by Kaspersky this week, targeted a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia and i… ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/netamloader-malware-targets-government.html))

### SMS of Death: Android under attack, an invisible SMS can block calls and emergency services
SMS of Death lets attackers crash Android call services with a hidden, zero-click message, blocking phone calls, even emergency calls too. A specially manipulated SMS message is enough to crash Android’s phone service, interrupt ongoing calls, and temporarily render the smartphone unusable. ([Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/202184/security/sms-of-death-android-under-attack-an-invisible-sms-can-block-calls-and-emergency-services.html))

### NIST Now Scores Only A Fraction Of New CVEs, And Your Risk Tools May Not Know
Since April 2026, NIST has scored only CVEs under active exploitation and those affecting software the US government depends on. Every other record arrives in the NVD with no NIST score, and the API marks many of them Deferred. ([/r/cybersecurity](https://www.reddit.com/r/cybersecurity/comments/1xl76fy/nist_now_scores_only_a_fraction_of_new_cves_and/))
